assumptions: Assumes the portal view is scoped to a specific child rather than anonymized aggregate data.

title: Portal records can serve as attributable evidence about the child's performance and submissions
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history are attributable records that can later be used as evidence that a particular child submitted work, received feedback, or obtained certain grades, reducing deniability around those facts.
assumptions: Assumes the records are tied to a specific student identity within the portal.

title: Portal response reveals the existence of a child's academic records
description: The system response itself reveals that records exist for a particular child, including whether grades, feedback, or submission history are present. An observer with access to the parent session could detect the existence and status of the child's academic activity from the response.
assumptions: Assumes the portal distinguishes between available and unavailable records in its responses.

title: Portal may disclose more detailed academic history than necessary to the parent
description: Displaying grades together with detailed feedback and full submission history may exceed the minimum granularity needed for the parent-facing purpose, especially if older submissions or detailed teacher comments are not strictly necessary for routine parental oversight.
assumptions: Assumes some of the detailed feedback or historical submission data may not be strictly required for the intended parent portal function.
uncertainty_note: Whether this is excessive depends on school policy and the legitimate scope of parental access, which is not fully specified.

title: Child may be unaware that detailed academic records are disclosed to the parent
description: At the destination, the parent receives the child's grades, feedback, and submission history. This can create unawareness for the child as data subject if the child is not clearly informed that these detailed records are accessible to the parent through the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the child is the primary data subject and may not receive clear notice about parent access.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state whether the child is informed about this disclosure.

title: Sharing detailed student records with a parent may lack an appropriate lawful basis or exceed permitted scope
description: Providing a parent with a child's grades, feedback, and submission history may create a compliance risk if the recipient is not legally entitled to all disclosed details, or if the scope of disclosure exceeds what is lawful under the applicable education/privacy regime.
assumptions: Assumes there may be cases such as mature minors, custody restrictions, or policy limits on parental access.
uncertainty_note: Applicable law and school policy are not provided, so this is a contextual compliance risk rather than a certain violation.

title: Administrator submits directly linkable identifiers for multiple related individuals
description: The school administrator shares names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. Names and emails are direct or near-direct identifiers, and the relationship data links records of parents and children together, enabling straightforward linkage of account records across administrative actions.
assumptions: The portal uses submitted names/emails/relationship fields to create or update persistent account records.

title: Portal can link parent and child records across accounts and roles
description: On receipt of account and relationship data, the web app can combine data of different individuals to maintain parent-child links and role assignments. This creates a privacy threat because records about students, parents, and administrators become linkable within the portal.
assumptions: The destination stores and processes relationship mappings between multiple individuals.

title: Administrator provides identified personal data
description: The administrator sends names and emails when creating or modifying accounts and links. This is identified information about parents and possibly students or staff, so the flow contains directly identifying personal data.

title: Data flow carries identified account-management data in transit
description: The transmitted payload includes names, emails, roles, and family relationship information, which are identified or readily identifiable personal data while in transit on DF12.

title: Portal processes identified account and relationship data
description: The destination process receives and processes identified personal data to create, modify, disable accounts, and maintain parent-child links.

title: Submitted account-management records can be attributed to the administrator
description: Administrative changes to accounts and parent-child links are likely attributable to the administrator who submitted them. The content of the request and resulting records may later be used as evidence that the administrator performed or authorized specific actions.
assumptions: Administrative actions are associated with the acting administrator's session or account.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention audit logs or signatures, so attribution is inferred from typical account-management behavior.

title: Portal processing creates attributable side effects for administrative actions
description: Creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and relationship links typically causes side effects such as changed account states and relationship mappings. These side effects can make the administrator's actions non-deniable.
assumptions: The portal persists account state changes in a way that can be tied back to the initiating administrator.
uncertainty_note: No explicit logging or audit mechanism is described; this threat is based on normal persistence of admin actions.

title: Administrator may disclose more sensitive relationship data than strictly necessary
description: The flow includes parent-child relationships in addition to names, emails, and roles. Family relationship data can be sensitive, and if the portal does not strictly require the full relationship detail for account administration, the source's sharing creates unnecessary disclosure risk.
assumptions: Some account-management tasks may not require full relationship details for every operation.
uncertainty_note: Necessity cannot be fully determined from the description alone; the threat applies if relationship details are sent for operations that do not require them.

title: Relationship and role data may be implicitly disclosed in transit as a side effect of account administration
description: Even when the explicit purpose is account management, the transmitted combination of names, emails, roles, and parent-child links implicitly reveals family structure and role assignments during the flow.

title: Portal may propagate account and family-link data beyond what is needed
description: Once received, the web app may make names, emails, roles, and parent-child links accessible to additional internal components or services beyond the immediate account-management function, increasing disclosure risk.
assumptions: The portal may integrate with other components or modules.
uncertainty_note: The description does not explicitly mention onward sharing or integrations; this is a plausible destination-side disclosure risk rather than a confirmed behavior.

title: Administrator may share others' personal data without those data subjects being aware
description: The administrator submits names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships about parents and children. Those data subjects may not be aware that their personal data and family links are being created, modified, or disabled through this administrative flow.

title: Portal processing may limit rectification or erasure of incorrect account-link data
description: If the portal receives and stores incorrect names, emails, roles, or parent-child links, affected data subjects may lack a direct way to rectify or remove that data, especially where changes are mediated only through administrators.
assumptions: Data subjects do not directly control administrative account and relationship records in the portal.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify available self-service controls or correction workflows.

title: Portal may not provide sufficient data subject controls over account and relationship data
description: Because the portal processes personal data and family relationships through administrator actions, affected parents or children may lack adequate rights mechanisms to access, rectify, or erase their data, creating a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Data subject rights handling is limited or mediated solely by administrators.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance risk inferred from the administrative nature of the flow; the actual rights-management features are not described.

title: Portal may process more personal data than necessary for account administration
description: If the destination processes names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships beyond what is strictly needed for creating, modifying, or disabling accounts, the flow contributes to a data minimization non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Not every administrative operation requires all listed attributes.
uncertainty_note: The exact minimum data needed for each operation is not specified.

title: Writing unique account identifiers enables linkage across records
description: The grading service writes account records into the account directory, and such records typically contain unique account identifiers. By sharing those identifiers, P2 enables records about the same student, parent, or related account to be linked across services and over time.

title: Directory can link parent and child accounts through stored relationship data
description: The account directory receives and stores explicit parent-child relationship links. This allows DS3 to combine data of different individuals and maintain relational graphs that link family members together.

title: Grading service writes identified account data
description: The flow writes account records to the directory. Account records and parent-child links imply processing of identified or directly attributable personal data rather than anonymous data.
uncertainty_note: The exact fields are not listed, but 'account records' in an account directory strongly suggests directly identified or uniquely attributable data.

title: Directory stores identifiers that make data subjects identifiable
description: By receiving account records and relationship links, the account directory stores unique references to students, parents, or guardians, making the involved data subjects identifiable within the system.

title: Stored account and relationship records can serve as attributable evidence
description: Once written to the account directory, account records and parent-child links may be used as evidence that a particular person held an account status or relationship in the system, reducing deniability regarding those claims.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the directory is treated as authoritative evidence for account ownership or family relationships.

title: Parent-child relationship data may disclose sensitive relationship information in transit
description: This flow carries not only account records but also explicit parent-child relationship links. Family relationship data can be more sensitive than minimally necessary identifiers, creating a disclosure risk if the full relationship detail is transmitted or exposed in transit.
uncertainty_note: The necessity of transmitting full relationship details cannot be fully assessed from the flow description alone.

title: Propagation of grading-originated account data to the directory may exceed necessity
description: The grading service propagates account records and family links into a separate account directory. If the directory does not strictly need all of these fields for its function, this constitutes unnecessary propagation of personal data to another repository.
uncertainty_note: The description does not specify the minimum data needed by DS3, so necessity is inferred rather than proven.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that grading data updates family-linked directory records
description: Students and parents may not expect that the grading service writes account records and explicit parent-child links into the account directory. This creates a risk that the involved data subjects are unaware of this storage and disclosure step.

title: Data subjects may lack ability to correct or remove incorrect relationship links
description: If DS3 stores parent-child relationship links received from the grading service, affected students or parents may have limited ability to rectify incorrect links or erase outdated relationship data once written.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state whether rectification or erasure mechanisms exist; this is a plausible risk arising from directory storage.

title: Writing full account and family-link data may violate data minimization
description: If the account directory receives more account detail or relationship information than is necessary for directory purposes, the processing may violate the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: This depends on DS3's legitimate purpose and required schema, which are not fully specified.

title: Insufficient support for rectification or erasure of directory relationship data
description: Because DS3 stores account and parent-child relationship records, inadequate mechanisms to access, correct, or remove those records would create a data-subject-rights compliance risk.
uncertainty_note: The existence of rights-handling mechanisms is not described; this is a compliance risk contingent on missing controls.

title: Backup export includes unique identifiers that enable cross-record linking
description: The nightly backup ships full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud hosting provider. Because the dataset includes account-directory identifiers and full student records, the source's act of sharing enables the recipient to link multiple records and activities to the same individual across backups and data domains.

title: Cloud provider can link individuals across combined backup datasets
description: On receipt of full grade records, assignments, and account-directory data, the cloud hosting provider can combine these attributes to link records belonging to the same student, instructor, or account holder, and potentially correlate them across replicated environments or backup snapshots.

title: Source discloses identified personal data in full backups
description: The source process sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third party. These data categories strongly imply direct identifiers and identified educational records are being processed and disclosed as part of the backup flow.

title: Backup transfer metadata may contain identified information
description: The backup and replication flow to the cloud provider may expose identified information in filenames, object names, routing metadata, tenant labels, or account references associated with the transfer, even aside from the payload contents.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention transfer metadata contents; this threat is plausible for hosted backup pipelines but not certain from the provided context alone.

title: Cloud provider receives and processes identified educational records
description: By receiving full backups containing grade records, assignments, and account-directory data, the destination processes identified or readily identifiable personal data belonging to students, instructors, and account holders.

title: Backed-up grade and assignment records can serve as attributable evidence
description: Full grade records and assignment data can be attributed to specific students and instructors, making the source's disclosure capable of preserving evidence about submissions, grading outcomes, and account ownership that may later be used to deny deniability.

title: Backup-transfer metadata may create attributable evidence of user records
description: Metadata associated with nightly backup and replication, such as timestamps, account references, dataset names, or job identifiers, can reinforce attribution of records or actions to particular individuals or accounts.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the actual backup tooling and metadata retained in transit; the description supports plausibility but not certainty.

title: Stored backups at the provider preserve attributable evidence
description: Once stored by the cloud hosting provider, the full backup can act as durable evidence tying educational records, submissions, and grades to specific individuals, reducing their ability to repudiate those records later.

title: Regular backup traffic can reveal the existence of educational records
description: A nightly recurring transfer of full backups to the cloud provider creates observable communications whose timing, size, and recurrence can reveal that grade records, assignments, and account-directory data exist and are being actively maintained.

title: Full backup includes highly sensitive educational data beyond minimal hosting need
description: The source sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party hosting provider. Educational records and account-directory data are sensitive, and sending the full dataset may exceed what is strictly necessary for backup/replication if more selective or minimized backup content could suffice.

title: Excessive amount of personal data is transferred in nightly full backups
description: The flow explicitly ships full records rather than a minimized subset, increasing disclosure by volume. This creates a data-disclosure threat because more personal data is processed and exposed than may be functionally necessary for resilient hosting.

title: Nightly replication may process personal data more frequently than necessary
description: The described nightly backup and hosting replication repeatedly transfers the full dataset to the provider. If less frequent backups or differential replication would satisfy operational needs, the source's chosen frequency causes unnecessary repeated disclosure.
uncertainty_note: The necessity of nightly full backups depends on recovery objectives and architecture, which are not provided.

title: Personal data is propagated to an external provider
description: The source propagates full educational and account-directory data to a third-party cloud hosting provider. This expands exposure to another service boundary and is a disclosure threat if the external propagation is broader than functionally necessary.

title: Sensitive records are shared with a predetermined external party
description: The flow makes personal data accessible to a fixed third party, the cloud hosting provider. Sharing full grade, assignment, and directory data with this predetermined external party increases exposure and may exceed necessity depending on the hosting arrangement.

title: Provider-side backup retention may keep personal data longer than needed
description: Once the cloud hosting provider receives nightly backups and replicated data, it may retain snapshots, replicas, or recovery copies for extended periods, creating disclosure risk through prolonged storage beyond functional necessity.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify the provider's retention schedule, so the duration aspect is inferred from common backup practices.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their educational records are replicated to a third-party host
description: Students and instructors whose grades, assignments, and directory data are included in the nightly backup may not be aware that their personal data is disclosed to and stored with a third-party cloud hosting provider.

title: Third-party backup storage can limit rectification or erasure control
description: Once personal data is stored in provider backups and replicas, data subjects may have limited practical ability to rectify or erase outdated or incorrect records from all copies held by the destination.

title: Full third-party backup may violate data minimization expectations
description: Sending full grade records, assignments, and account-directory data to the cloud hosting provider may process more personal data than is necessary for the stated backup and replication purpose, creating a regulatory noncompliance risk under data minimization principles.

title: Third-party hosting transfer may lack an appropriate lawful basis or safeguards
description: Disclosing complete educational records and account-directory data to an external cloud hosting provider may be unlawful if the organization lacks an appropriate lawful basis, contractual safeguards, or other required protections for this third-party processing.
uncertainty_note: The existence of a lawful basis, processor agreement, and jurisdictional safeguards is not provided, so this is a conditional compliance threat rather than a confirmed violation.

title: Provider backup retention may conflict with storage limitation requirements
description: If the cloud hosting provider retains backup copies, replicas, or snapshots longer than necessary for the hosting purpose, the destination's processing can create a storage-limitation noncompliance risk.
uncertainty_note: Retention duration is not specified in the flow description; this threat depends on actual provider retention and deletion controls.

title: Provider-held backups may undermine fulfillment of data subject rights
description: Storing personal data in third-party backups and replicas can make it difficult to honor access, rectification, or erasure requests across all copies, creating a risk of insufficient support for data subject rights.

title: Grade records shared with stable student identifiers enable cross-view linkage
description: The grade records database is the source of records used to build student, parent, and teacher views. If the records include stable student identifiers, the act of sharing them from DS2 enables linking the same student's data across those different views and contexts.

title: Assignment & Grading Service can link records across students, parents, and teachers
description: Because P2 reads grade records to build multiple audience-specific views, it may combine records about students with related parent and teacher context, enabling linkage across different individuals connected through the educational relationship.

title: Database shares identified grade records
description: Grade records used to build student, parent, and teacher views are likely to contain directly identified information such as student names or IDs. By sharing these records, DS2 causes identified personal data to be processed.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not enumerate fields, so direct identifiers are inferred from the stated purpose of building audience-specific grade views.

title: Data flow likely carries unique identifiers for students and related parties
description: The flow from DS2 to P2 likely contains unique references such as student IDs, assignment IDs tied to a student, or account-linked identifiers needed to assemble the views, making data subjects identifiable in transit.
uncertainty_note: Identifiers are likely needed for view construction, but the exact payload is not specified.

title: Received grade records can serve as attributable evidence about a student's performance
description: Once P2 receives and processes grade records, those records can be used as evidence attributable to a specific student, making it harder for the student to deny claims about grades, submissions, or academic standing represented in the data.

title: Observation of grade-record retrieval can reveal that grade information exists for a subject
description: The existence of this read flow from the grade records database to the grading service may allow an observer of communications to detect that grade records are being accessed for some student or class context, revealing the existence of an item of interest.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the flow or its metadata is observable to an attacker or unauthorized party.

title: Database may disclose more grade-record data than needed for view generation
description: DS2 may provide full grade records when P2 only needs a subset of fields to build student, parent, and teacher views. Sharing complete records instead of minimally necessary attributes would disclose an excessive amount of personal data.
uncertainty_note: The exact schema and whether field-level minimization is applied are not provided.

title: Service processing supports disclosure to multiple predetermined parties
description: P2 reads grade records specifically to build views for students, parents, and teachers. This indicates the destination processes the data for access by a predetermined set of parties, which may expose personal data to more parties than strictly necessary if role-based scoping is not minimal.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on whether each party truly needs the same underlying grade-record scope; the description only confirms multiple recipient categories.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their grade records are reused to generate multiple audience views
description: At P2, grade records are processed to build views for students, parents, and teachers. Students and possibly parents may not be fully aware that the same underlying records are reused and disclosed in these different contexts.
uncertainty_note: Awareness depends on notices and user expectations, which are not described.

title: View-generation processing may violate data minimization if full records are used
description: If P2 reads more personal data from grade records than is necessary to construct each audience-specific view, the destination's processing could violate the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: This is contingent on the actual fields retrieved and whether audience-specific minimization is implemented.
